disease_label_per_paper: Exertional heat stroke with multiorgan failure and bimodal rhabdomyolysis
presentation_summary: 27-year-old male athlete lost consciousness after running 6.8 km at 34 C ambient temperature without hydration support while recovering from recent gastroenteritis.
At emergency assessment, GCS was 7, BP 70/40 mmHg, HR 162/min, RR 30/min, SpO2 98% on room air, and tympanic temperature 40.2 C.
Initial labs included creatinine 1.81 mg/dL, BUN 32.21 mg/dL, sodium 144 mmol/L, potassium 5.1 mmol/L, bicarbonate 17 mmol/L, CK total 312 U/L, INR 1.61, and pH 7.406 with HCO3 18.7.

After two days of initial improvement, he developed recurrent shock, anuria, desaturation to 83%, intubation, vasopressors, CRRT, DIC requiring cryoprecipitate/FFP, and acute liver failure physiology.
ALT and AST reached 8287 U/L and 4743 U/L respectively, with total bilirubin 12.07 mg/dL; he improved with supportive management without liver transplant and was discharged stable.
